name: demo_spare_key
title: My landlord wanted to charge me for the lock he told me to replace
body: This is a fictional test story. I rent a small flat above a shop. Last month my front door key snapped inside the lock while I was coming home from work. I called my landlord from the stairs. He said he was out of town, told me to get a locksmith, and asked me to send him the receipt so he could reimburse me. I texted him to confirm before calling anyone, and he replied yes. The locksmith replaced the cylinder that evening. I sent the receipt and gave the shop downstairs a sealed envelope with the spare key, as my landlord requested. Two weeks later he emailed a list of deductions he planned to take from my deposit when my tenancy ended. One was for an unauthorized lock change. Another was for failing to provide a spare key. I called him and he said he would never authorize a tenant to change a lock. I forwarded the text conversation, including his instructions about the envelope. He said the texts only authorized calling a locksmith, not replacing anything. I asked how a locksmith was supposed to fix a key snapped inside a damaged cylinder without replacing it. He did not answer that question. Instead he said he still had not received a spare. I went downstairs to ask the shopkeeper. She took out the envelope. It had not been collected. I photographed the envelope on the counter and emailed the picture to my landlord with the shop's opening hours. The next morning he replied with a revised deductions list. Both lock charges were gone. He also said the reimbursement would be included with my next rent statement. I have kept the messages and the receipt. I am relieved the charges are gone, but I no longer handle anything with him by phone unless I follow it with a text.
